title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page shows that 'Q' there means a combinatorial square (carré), not a field (corps). Its automorphism group is the dihedral group 𝔻_4 of order 8, with exact sequence 1→F_2→𝔻_4→F_2^2→1. Grothendieck had asked whether the remark Aut(𝔻_4)≅𝔻_4 hides an equivalence (squares) ≃ (groups isomorphic to 𝔻_4) that is NOT Q ↦ Aut(Q). This page constructs that equivalence.

(1) The construction. Let D ≅ 𝔻_4 and let a be its unique central element ≠1. Let S be the set of elements of order 2 other than a, i.e. the four non-central involutions (in ⟨r,s⟩: s, sr, sr², sr³). Multiplication by the central element, x ↦ x' := xa, is a fixed-point-free involution of S. The pairs are {s, sr²} and {sr, sr³}. A combinatorial square on a 4-element vertex set is the same as a fixed-point-free involution (the antipodism): the diagonals are the antipodal pairs and the edges are the other four pairs. So D gives a square Q_D with vertex set S, antipodism x ↦ x', and edges the non-commuting pairs {x,y} with y ≠ x, x'.

(2) The equivalence. The claim is that D ↦ Q_D is an equivalence of groupoids (groups ≅ 𝔻_4, isomorphisms) → (combinatorial squares, isomorphisms). Both groupoids are connected, so it suffices to check that Aut(D) → Aut(Q_D) is bijective.
- Aut(D) acts on S and fixes a, so it respects the antipodism.
- The action is faithful, since s and sr generate D.
- |Aut(𝔻_4)| = 8 = |Aut(square)|.
Hence the map is bijective. Concretely, inner automorphisms (≅ F_2^2) preserve each antipodal pair, and the outer class swaps the two pairs.

(3) The quasi-inverse. D is recovered from (S, x ↦ x') by generators x ∈ S and a, with relations [x,y] = a for y ≠ x, x'. Check: [s, sr] = r s r⁻¹ s = r² = a.

(4) Marginal NB (reconstructed). For a square Q, the group D = Aut(Q) ≅ 𝔻_4 has central element equal to the antipodism (rotation by π). But Q_{Aut Q} is not Q. Its vertices are the four reflection axes of Q (two diagonals, two medians), and its antipodism pairs perpendicular axes, i.e. the partition 'C ∐ D' of the previous page. So Q_{Aut(Q)} is a different square, the 45°-rotated or 'dual' one. This is why the equivalence is not Q ↦ Aut(Q).

(5) Linear-algebra description, preparing the next page.
- Any 4-element set S is canonically a torsor under the Klein group V_S ≅ F_2^2 of double transpositions, i.e. an affine F_2-plane.
- A square structure on S is a fixed-point-free involution, i.e. a partition of type (2,2). Equivalently it is a nonzero vector of V_S, or a line, or (via the canonical alternating form, Λ²V_S ≅ F_2) a nonzero a_S ∈ V_S^*.
- The next page converts (V, α) into a 2-element set C with V ≅ F_2^C, and S into a double cover A → C with S = sections, i.e. S = ∏_c A_c.

Purpose in the manuscript. This is preparatory combinatorics for the 2-torsion / level-2 structures in the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2. The four branch points of x : E → P^1 form a torsor under E[2]. A choice of partition of type (2,2) corresponds to a nonzero 2-torsion point (a Γ_0(2)-type structure), with the 𝔻_4 ⊂ S_4 stabilizers.
errors: The presentation D = ⟨x∈S, a | [x,y]=a for y≠x,x'⟩ is incomplete as written: one must also impose x² = 1, a² = 1, a central and x' = xa (or treat a and x ↦ x' as given data); otherwise the group defined is larger.

'a_S ∈ V_S^*' should be a nonzero element. Strictly, the fixed-point-free involution is a nonzero vector of V_S; identifying it with a nonzero linear form uses the canonical isomorphism V_S ≅ V_S^* for rank 2 over F_2. This is harmless but implicit.

Not an error, but the equivalence claim is asserted without proof. The verification (Aut(𝔻_4) acts faithfully on the 4 non-central involutions, preserving the pairing, and both groups have order 8) is immediate.

ideas.what: Equivalence of groupoids between groups isomorphic to D_4 and combinatorial squares, via the set of non-central involutions with the pairing x ↦ xa
ideas.modern_name: Aut(D_4) ≅ D_4 / the outer automorphism of D_4 exchanging the two reflection classes; groupoid equivalence of torsor categories

ideas.what: Q_{Aut(Q)} is the 'dual' square of axes, not Q itself, so Q ↦ Aut(Q) is not the inverse equivalence
ideas.modern_name: non-inner (outer) automorphism of D_4; the 45° rotation exchanging vertex-reflections and edge-reflections

ideas.what: Presentation of D_4 from a 4-set with fixed-point-free involution: generators the vertices, commutators of adjacent vertices equal to the central element
ideas.modern_name: presentation of D_4 as a central extension of F_2^2 by F_2 (commutator form)

ideas.what: A 4-element set is canonically an F_2-affine plane (torsor under the Klein group); a square structure is a nonzero vector / linear form, i.e. a (2,2)-partition
ideas.modern_name: S_4 → S_3 = GL_2(F_2) with kernel V_4; level-2 structures

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, well-known finite group combinatorics (D_4 ↔ squares, Aut(D_4) ≅ D_4, the dual square of axes), done in Grothendieck's characteristic 'torsor/groupoid' style as groundwork for level-2 structures on elliptic curves. Nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'Si D est un groupe quaternionique : 𝔻_4' should read 'Si D est un groupe isomorphe à 𝔻_4'. It is the dihedral group: the quaternion group has only one element of order 2, while here S has four.
'est un quatre éléments' should read 'est un ens. à quatre éléments'.
'x ↦ x+a' is probably 'x ↦ xa' (product with the central element); the page is written multiplicatively.
'Mais la foncteur' should read 'Mais le foncteur'.
'Si on peut, pour décrire la structure de carré' is probably 'Si on veut, pour décrire la structure de carré'.
'd'une str. de — i.e. d'un torseur' is likely 'd'une structure de plan affine (sur F_2) — i.e. d'un torseur'.
'{+quadratique+}' is likely 'd'une involution sans points fixes' (cf. the end of the sentence 'sans points fixes de S, i.e. d'une partition de type (2,2)').
Previous page: 'corps épinglé Q_0' / 'quaternions (corps)' should almost certainly be 'carré' (square), not 'corps'.

Margin NB is roughly: 'NB Si on part d'un carré Q, D = Aut(Q) ≅ 𝔻_4, l'antipodisme est l'élément central de D, et l'on trouve pour Q_D un carré différent de Q (dont les sommets sont les axes C ∐ D)...'.
